seeds.proposal: Repeat the legal Daemon attack twice: first sacrifices Ping, second captures Kernel.
Trace shoots the guarded Kernel twice without relocating. Bodyguard redirect blocks ordinary search depth.
Two adjacent guards require three repeated hits. Ping is sacrificed before Ice; avoid claiming a two-action repeat win.
Ice captures the sole guard directly at (3,4), then the adjacent Kernel. First action changes occupancy and source.
Find an orthogonal Ping approach then a diagonal Kernel capture; compare static attack-map and two-action reasoning.
Daemon relocates orthogonally then shoots an adjacent diagonal Kernel. Adjacent shots use all eight directions.
Trace makes one orthogonal step to create a diagonal shot of legal minimum range two.
Move the friendly Trace out of Daemon's line, then Daemon captures Kernel. The first mover is not the final attacker.
Exploit jumps off the diagonal between Ice and enemy Kernel, enabling an immediate second-action capture.
Ping moves orthogonally off Trace's diagonal; Trace then shoots the Kernel at range three.
Moving the sole adjacent guard away may expose approach-plus-capture. Exact next-turn safety must classify every legal action.
Same board with two actions: an exposed first move may be repairable. Do not transfer last-action loss labels unchanged.
Cyan ending round-eight turn does not shrink immediately, but its edge Kernel cannot move again before Magenta ends the round.
Magenta must move its edge Kernel inward unless it can terminate first. Last-action timing is exact.
A quiet Trace move leaves both Kernels burning; Magenta wins the simultaneous-burn tiebreak.
Immediate Kernel capture wins while own Kernel is stranded on the ring that burns after the opponent turn.
Two king steps can capture before bare-Kernel adjudication. Chebyshev distance two is within current-turn reach.
One step cannot capture at distance two; final proximity at most two loses, so legal retreat destinations must be checked.
Exact bare-Kernel result depends on final distance and center ring, with equal rings favoring Magenta.
Same geometry and clock with Cyan to move tests the tie asymmetry; it cannot be removed by canonical rotation.
Adjacent enemy Ping blocks Trace and cannot be shot by Trace. Daemon can shoot the blocker before Trace's long shot.
Tempting Kernel capture may walk out of guard range into Daemon's two-action approach. Compare actual post-action safety.
On the already shrunken board, ring one burns now; the apparent outer board edge is irrelevant.
Final two-by-two board: compare guard redirection, immediate capture and simultaneous-burn tie. Adjudication must use exact engine order.
